newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia coal exports seen rising-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia coal exports seen rising-ABARE.

text.p: Australia's total coal export earnings are projected to increase to A$8.7 billion in 2001/02 ending June 30 because of strong export volumes, Lindsay Hogan, senior research economist from the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Research Economics (ABARE), said on Thursday.
This is based on average annual export increases of 4.3 percent to 180 million tonnes in 2001/02 from 146 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Addressing the ABARE Outlook conference here, Hogan said the projected growth in export values was despite an expected slight fall in real coal prices.
The major growth in exports would be from thermal coal, she said.
Australia's total coal exports were expected to increase from A$6.9 billion in 1994/95. This was down from A$7.2 billion the year before.

This is based on exports of 73.3 million tonnes of coking coal in 1994/95, up from 69.9 million tonnes the year before, and 62.9 million tonnes of thermal coal in 1994/95, up from 59.2 million tonnes the year before.
Hogan's forecasts show coking coal exports are expected to rise to A$4.8 billion in 1996/97, up 1.2 percent on 1995/96.
This is based on exports of 79.0 million tonnes, up 2.1 percent from the year before.
Thermal coal exports are expected to rise to A$3.1 billion in 1996/97, up 4.3 percent on the year before, based on exports of 66.7 million tonnes in 1996/97, up 9.2 percent on 1995/96.
Hogan predicted that competition would increase in annual pricing negotiations, with published prices likely to improve the efficiency of the coal market.
